question_types.description: Short-answer conceptual questions on good R scripts, reproducibility, and AI use.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give two reasons we use R in addition to Excel, and one situation where Excel is still better.
parts.answer: R: reproducible, scales past 1M rows, version-controllable, composable, stronger stats. Excel: quick ad-hoc work, interactive workbooks for non-technical colleagues, formatted tables.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain what <- does and what c() does.
parts.answer: <- assigns a value to a variable; c() combines values into a vector.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A colleague edited the CSV in Excel then re-ran their R script and got a different answer. Why is this a reproducibility problem, and how do you avoid it?
parts.answer: The data was changed outside the script, so the script no longer fully records the analysis. Fix: do all cleaning in the script, reading the raw unedited CSV.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Describe one task where an AI assistant helps, and one where relying on it could mislead you.
parts.answer: Helps: scaffolding, explaining errors, recalling function names, boilerplate. Misleads: wrong column assumptions, outdated syntax, code that runs but answers the wrong question. Safeguard: understand every line before running.

parts.label: a
parts.text: List three habits of a well-written R script.
parts.answer: Any three: header comment; libraries at top; comments explain why not what; descriptive names; named steps; re-runnable from scratch; test on a subset first.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A script computes mean(wheat$yield_bu_ac) and gets NA. Most likely cause and one-argument fix?
parts.answer: The column has missing values (NA), which mean() propagates. Fix: add na.rm = TRUE.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain what 're-runnable from scratch' means and why the course insists on it.
parts.answer: Clearing the environment, restarting R, and running top-to-bottom reproduces the same results with no manual steps. It is the working definition of reproducibility.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Why does the course allow AI on assignments but not on tests?
parts.answer: Assignments build responsible-AI-use skills; tests verify that the understanding is the student's own, not the tool's.
